content:

Lesson 3: Types of Arguments: Deduction and Induction

Lesson Overview: Arguments are divided into two primary classes based on the strength of their inferential claim: Deductive Arguments and Inductive Arguments. The central distinction lies in whether the conclusion is claimed to follow from the premises with absolute necessity or merely with probability.

👉 Lesson Overview:
በዚህ ትምህርት ውስጥ አርጉመንቶችን በሁለት ዋና ዋና ክፍሎች እንከፍላቸዋለን:: እነሱም Deductive Arguments እና Inductive Arguments ናቸው:: በሁለቱ መካከል ያለው ዋና ልዩነት ማስረጃው (Premise) ለድምዳሜው (Conclusion) የሚሰጠው የሐሳብ ጥንካሬ ወይም ትስስር መጠን ነው:: ድምዳሜው በፍጹም እርግጠኝነት (Necessity) ይከተላል ወይስ በይሆናልነት (Probability) የሚለውን በዝርዝር እንመረምራለን::

3.1 Deductive Arguments

A deductive argument is an argument incorporating the claim that it is impossible for the conclusion to be false given that the premises are true. In such arguments, the conclusion is claimed to follow necessarily and conclusively from the premises. Deductive reasoning involves a claim of absolute certainty.

Example 1:
All philosophers are critical thinkers.
Socrates is a philosopher.
Therefore, Socrates is a critical thinker.

Example 2:
All African footballers are blacks.
Messi is an African footballer.
It follows that, Messi is black.

In both examples, if we assume the premises are true, it is logically impossible for the conclusion to be false. Even if a premise contains factual inaccuracies in reality (e.g., claiming Messi is an African footballer), the structure itself claims strict necessity.

👉 Deductive Arguments :
በ Deductive Argument ውስጥ "ማስረጃዎቹ (Premises) እውነት ከሆኑ ድምዳሜው (Conclusion) በፍጹም ሐሰት ሊሆን አይችልም!" የሚል ጠንካራ አቋም አለ:: እዚህ ጋር ዋናው ቁልፍ ነገር Strict Necessity (100% እርግጠኝነት) ነው::

• ምሳሌ 1 ፡ ፈላስፎች በሙሉ Critical Thinkers ከሆኑ እና ሶቅራጥስ ፈላስፋ ከሆነ፣ ሶቅራጥስ Critical Thinker አለመሆን አይችልም!
• ምሳሌ 2 ፡ እውነታው ላይ ሜሲ የአፍሪካ ኳስ ተጫዋች ባይሆንም፣ በአርጉመንቱ መዋቅር መሠረት ግን ማስረጃዎቹ እውነት ናቸው ብለን ብንቀበል ድምዳሜው የግድ እውነት መሆን አለበት:: Logic ላይ የሚያስፈልገን የሐሳቡ መዋቅራዊ ትስስር (Structural Link) እንጂ በገሀዱ ዓለም ያለው እውነታ ነገር አይደለም::

3.2 Inductive Arguments

An inductive argument is an argument incorporating the claim that it is improbable for the conclusion to be false given that the premises are true. The premises provide evidence that supports the conclusion with a degree of probability rather than strict necessity.

Example 1:
Most African leaders are blacks.
Mandela was an African leader.
Therefore, probably Mandela was black.

Example 2:
Almost all women are mammals.
Hanan is a woman.
Hence, Hanan is a mammal.

In inductive arguments, even if all premises are assumed true, it remains logically possible for the conclusion to be false, though improbable.

👉 Inductive Arguments :
በ Inductive Argument ውስጥ ማስረጃዎቹ እውነት ቢሆኑ እንኳ ድምዳሜው በይሆናልነት (Probability) እንጂ በፍጹም እርግጠኝነት አይከተልም:: ድምዳሜው ሐሰት የመሆን እድል ሁልጊዜም ቢሆን ትንሽም ብትሆን አለች::

• ምሳሌ 1 ፡ አብዛኞቹ የአፍሪካ መሪዎች ጥቁር ስለሆኑና ማንዴላ የአፍሪካ መሪ ስለነበር ማንዴላ ጥቁር የመሆን እድሉ ከፍተኛ ነው (Probable)፤ ነገር ግን ነጭ የመሆን ትንሽ እድል ነበረው:: ስለዚህ ይሄ Inductive ነው::
• ምሳሌ 2 ፡ ጊቢ ውስጥ "99% ተማሪዎች Dorm ገብተዋል" ብትባል፣ ፎቅ ላይ የምታገኘው ተማሪ Dorm የመግባት እድሉ ከፍተኛ እንጂ 100% እርግጠኛ አያደርግህም!

3.3 Differentiating Deductive and Inductive Arguments

To determine whether an argument is deductive or inductive, we examine three objective factors:

  • 1. The occurrence of special indicator words
  • 2. The actual strength of the inferential link between premises and conclusion
  • 3. The character or form of argumentation

1. Indicator Words

Deductive indicator words signal certainty: definitely, certainly, absolutely, necessarily.

Inductive indicator words signal probability: probably, likely, unlikely, plausible, implausible, reasonable to conclude.

💡 Exam Hint :
ተማሪዎች በፈተና ላይ ብዙ ጊዜ የሚሸወዱት በቃላት ነው! ለምሳሌ አንድ ተናጋሪ ለንግግር ማደመቂያ ሲል "It certainly follows that..." ብሎ ቢናገርም፣ የአርጉመንቱ ይዘት Inductive ከሆነ ቃሉን ትታችሁ ይዘቱን መገምገም አለባችሁ:: Rhetorical Indicator words ሊያታልሉ ስለሚችሉ የሐሳቡን ጥንካሬ (Strength) ተመልከቱ!

2. Actual Strength of the Inferential Link

If the conclusion follows with strict necessity, the argument is deductive regardless of indicator words. If it follows only with probability, it is inductive.

Deductive Link Example:
All Ethiopian people love their country. Debebe is an Ethiopian. Therefore, Debebe loves his country.
👉 Strict Necessity: It is impossible for Debebe not to love his country if the premises are true.

Inductive Link Example:
The majority of Ethiopian people are poor. Alamudin is an Ethiopian. Therefore, Alamudin is poor.
👉 Probability: Alamudin might be rich despite the majority being poor. Thus, it is inductive.

👉 Inferential Link :
ቃላቶቹ ቢኖሩም ባይኖሩም ዋናው ነገር የሐሳቡ ትስስር ነው:: በመጀመሪያው ምሳሌ "ሁሉም ኢትዮጵያዊ ሀገሩን ይወዳል" ከተባለ ደቡብ ሀገሩን አለመውደድ አይችልም (Strict Necessity) :: በሁለተኛው ምሳሌ ግን አላሙዲን ሀብታም ሊሆን ስለሚችል አርጉመንቱ Probable ብቻ ነው የሚሆነው::

3. Character or Form of Argumentation

When indicator words are absent and the strictness of the link is unclear, the structural form of the argument serves as the decisive factor.

Instances of Deductive Argumentative Forms

  • 1. Argument Based on Mathematics: Arguments where conclusions depend on purely arithmetic or geometric computation (excluding statistical arguments, which are inductive).
    👉 Example: Counting 2 oranges and 3 bananas to conclude there are 5 fruits in a bag.
  • 2. Argument Based on Definition: Arguments where the conclusion depends merely on the definition of a word or phrase used in the premise.
    👉 Example: Angel is honest; therefore, Angel tells the truth. (By definition of honest).
  • 3. Syllogisms: Arguments consisting of exactly two premises and one conclusion.
    • Categorical Syllogism: Statements starting with "All", "No", or "Some".
      👉 Example: All Egyptians are Muslims. No Muslim is a Christian. Hence, no Egyptian is a Christian.
    • Hypothetical Syllogism: Has a conditional ("if... then...") statement for one or both premises.
      👉 Example: If you study hard, then you will graduate with Distinction. If you graduate with Distinction, then you will get a rewarding job. Therefore, if you study hard, then you will get a rewarding job.
    • Disjunctive Syllogism: Contains an "either... or..." statement.
      👉 Example: Rewina is either Ethiopian or Eritrean. Rewina is not Eritrean. Therefore, Rewina is Ethiopian.

Instances of Inductive Argumentative Forms

  • 1. Prediction: Premises deal with a known past or present event, and the conclusion moves beyond to a future event.
    👉 Example: Dark clouds are developing in the highland; therefore, rain will fall within 24 hours.
  • 2. Argument from Analogy: Depends on a similarity between two things to conclude that a property of one applies to the other.
    👉 Example: Computer A and Computer B are manufactured in 2012 and easy to access. Computer A is fast; therefore, Computer B is fast.
  • 3. Inductive Generalization: Proceeds from knowledge of a selected sample to a claim about a whole group.
    👉 Example: Three out of four prisoners in a specific facility are black; therefore, three-fourths of all prison populations are black.
  • 4. Argument from Authority: Conclusion rests upon a statement made by a presumed authority or eyewitness.
    👉 Example: A University Professor claims that all matter is made of quarks; therefore, all matter is made of quarks.
  • 5. Argument Based on Signs: Proceeds from knowledge of a sign to knowledge of the condition symbolized by the sign.
    👉 Example: Seeing a 'No Parking' sign on the roadside and concluding parking is disallowed in that area.
  • 6. Causal Inference: Proceeds from knowledge of a cause to an effect, or from effect to cause.
    👉 Example (Cause to Effect): Leaving a water bottle in the freezer overnight and concluding it froze.
    👉 Example (Effect to Cause): Tasting dry chicken and concluding it was overcooked.

👉 የ Argument Forms የካምፓስ አዝናኝ ማብራሪያ:
• Argument from Definition: ጓደኛህ "ካፌ ምግቡ ሱፐር ነው" ቢልህና "ስለዚህ ምግቡ ቆንጆ ነው" ብትል በቃላት ፍቺ (Definition) መሠረት Deductive ነው!
• Argument Based on Signs: የካምፓሱ በር ላይ "Do Not Enter" የሚል ምልክት አቁመው ብታይ እና "እዚህ ጋር መግባት አይቻልም" ብለህ ብትደመድም Sign ስለሆነ Inductive ነው (ምክንያቱም ምልክቱ በስህተት ተቀምጦ ሊሆን ስለሚችል 100% እርግጠኝነት የለውም)!
• Causal Inference: ማታ ተኝተህ አርፍደህ ስትነቃ ዶርም ውስጥ መብራት ጠፍቶ ብታይ "ትራንስፎርመሩ ተበላሽቷል" ብትል ከውጤት ወደ ምክንያት (Effect to Cause) የሄደ Inductive Causal Inference ነው!

Furthermore Considerations & Generalization Forms

Scientific arguments can be inductive or deductive: discovering natural laws is generally inductive, while applying known laws to specific cases is deductive. Historically (Aristotelian view), deduction was defined as moving from general to particular, and induction from particular to general. However, modern logic recognizes exceptions:

Deductive (Particular to General):
Three is a prime number.
Five is a prime number.
Seven is a prime number.
Therefore, all odd numbers between two and eight are prime numbers.

Inductive (General to Particular):
All emeralds previously found have been green.
Therefore, the next emerald to be found will be green.

💡 Exam Hint :
በድሮ አባባል "Deduction ከ General ወደ Particular ነው፤ Induction ደግሞ ከ Particular ወደ General ነው" የሚለው ሁልጊዜ ትክክለኛ መለያ አይደለም! በዘመናዊ Logic መሠረት ብቸኛውና ትክክለኛው መለያ Inferential Strength (Necessity vs. Probability) ብቻ ነው!

📝 Practice Exam Questions

Question 1: A doctor examines a patient, sees a high body temperature and a rash, and concludes that the patient has a viral infection. This argument is best classified as:

A) Deductive, argument based on definition
B) Inductive, causal inference
C) Deductive, categorical syllogism
D) Inductive, argument from example

Answer: B
Explanation: Observing symptoms (effects) and concluding the presence of an infection (cause) is a causal inference, which is an inductive form.

👉 በሽተኛው ላይ የታዩትን ምልክቶች (ውጤት) በማየት መንስኤውን (ምክንያቱን) መገመት ከ Effect ወደ Cause የሚደረግ Causal Inference (Inductive) ነው::


Question 2: Which of the following is a deductive argument form?

A) Prediction
B) Argument from analogy
C) Disjunctive syllogism
D) Argument based on signs

Answer: C
Explanation: Disjunctive syllogism (either... or...) is one of the standard forms of deductive reasoning.

👉 Disjunctive syllogism ("either... or...") ከ Deductive Argument ዘሮች አንዱ ነው::


Question 3: "All squares are rectangles. A shape 'X' is a square. Therefore, shape 'X' is definitely a rectangle." This argument is:
A) Inductive because it makes a prediction
B) Deductive based on definition/mathematical property
C) Inductive based on authority
D) Deductive based on signs

Answer: B
Explanation: The conclusion follows with absolute necessity based on mathematical definition, making it a deductive argument.

👉 የቅርፁን ትርጓሜና የሂሳብ ህግ መሰረት በማድረግ ድምዳሜው በ 100% እርግጠኝነት ስለሚከተል Deductive ነው::
